question.text: Under reporting compliances for Cat I/II AIFs, which of the following statements about Form 64C and Form 64D is CORRECT?

answer.text: Form 64C goes to the Principal CIT and Form 64D goes to the unit-holder, both by 15 June.
Form 64C is a TDS return; Form 64D is the fund's ITR.
Only Form 64C is needed; Form 64D was abolished by Finance Act 2024.

Form 64C is furnished to the unit-holder by 30 June of the following FY; Form 64D is furnished electronically to the jurisdictional PCIT/CIT by 15 June, duly verified by a practicing Chartered Accountant under digital signature.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook Para 16.1.7: Form 64C is the statement of income paid/credited to the unit-holder, given to the UNIT-HOLDER by 30 June of the following FY. Form 64D is a similar electronic statement to the jurisdictional PCIT/CIT by 15 June, verified by a practicing CA under digital signature. These are the pass-through disclosure statements. The Trap: Option A swaps the recipients and the dates. Option B confuses these with TDS/ITR forms. Option C fabricates an abolition — Form 64D is very much alive. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C Compliance tests these forms directly. XIX-C expects the manager to own the timeline — missing 15 June attracts penalty under Section 271FAB. Manager's Pro-Tip: Start the Form 64D CA certification in April — don't wait for June. Your fund admin should auto-extract pass-through attribution per investor by head; getting a CA attestation on 500 LP records in June crunch season has real execution risk.
